newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FOCUS-OTP PRICE SEEN HOLDING WITH APV SALE.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-OTP PRICE SEEN HOLDING WITH APV SALE.

text.p: Hungary's privatisation agency APV's decision to sell its 25 percent stake in OTP Bank in one go could cause a temporary dip in the share price but will not affect it long-term, analysts said.

"I think there is going to be downward pressure on the price but that will be in the short term," said Antony Vago of Rababank. "The good thing is it's providing more liquidity for the stock and for the market in general and I think that is The combined sale of seven million ordinary shares will consist of a private placement for foreign and domestic instutional investors and a public offering for private domestic investors.
Financial advisors and lead managers for the offering will be London-based Schroders and Budapest-based Creditanstalt Ertekpapir Rt.
The offering is expected to take place in October after OTP has transferred one golden share to APV.

Rudi Voros of ICE Securities said that while the one-off share issue, worth $230 million at current prices, seemed large, APV were probably keen to offload the stake ahead of other planned bank issues elsewhere in central Europe.
"The Czech government is planning to sell off big chunks of the large commercial banks like Komercni Banka and Ceska Sporitelna ," he said.

"If interest picks up for Komercni, which is a larger bank than OTP, then it's going to be more difficult to place the stocks...while after the Polish elections there may be issues for some Polish banks."
Voros said that OTP's share proce is likely to keep its value until October as the company's fundamentals are strong.

"OTP's expensive because of the situation in the Czech Republic and Poland (but) it still has significant growth potential," he said. "It's a very prudent venture, very well capitalised and very well provisioned, unlike the Czech banks for instance.
"They're managing the restructuring process very well, with personal expenditure falling even in nominal terms," he added. "People accept now its a quality company."
Vago believes the timing of the sale is also connected with current rising markets throughout the region. Hungary's stocks have risen 80 percent this year in forint terms.
"It's definitely a good time (for the placement), the mood is still quite positive," he said.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange on Thursday, OTP shares closed unchanged at 6,400 forints.
